thesisQuality.note: Exceptional-band lower range: very large Cloud backlog and 48% Cloud growth demonstrate adoption/value capture, tempered by AI capex return uncertainty.

financialOperatingMomentum.note: Exceptional-band lower range: Cloud growth/backlog and broad cash-generating scale support strong momentum, tempered by $175B-$185B capex burden.

marketValuationOpportunity.note: Mixed band: about 17.6x trailing P/E is not extreme relative to current earnings, but ~$4.14T market cap and very high capex limit asymmetry.

catalystScore.note: Strong band: AI/Cloud backlog conversion and Intersect energy-development integration are identifiable material catalysts, with timing/execution uncertainty.

governancePower.note: Strong band: scale capital allocation includes deliberate vertical investment into energy constraints; high capex and acquisition execution prevent exceptional treatment.

alignment2036.note: Exceptional band: cloud, AI compute and energy infrastructure are foundational across multiple plausible 2036 digital-infrastructure futures.

crossDivisionLeverage.note: Exceptional band: Search/services, Cloud and infrastructure capabilities create multiple independent demand engines sharing AI/compute capability.

bottleneckControl.note: Strong band: Intersect adds multi-GW energy-development capability against a real power constraint, but Alphabet does not control grid/permitting bottlenecks outright.

scenarioRobustness.note: Exceptional-band lower range: diversified services and Cloud provide multiple monetization paths, tempered by common AI-capex exposure.

substitutionResilience.note: Exceptional-band lower range: ecosystem scale and vertically integrated compute/infrastructure create replacement friction, while rapid model/hardware shifts remain credible substitutes.

supplyChainResilience.note: Strong band: vertical energy-development action improves resilience, but grid, equipment, construction and permitting dependencies remain material.

pricingPower.note: Exceptional-band lower range: rapid Cloud growth and large backlog support durable value capture, but direct contract pass-through evidence is incomplete.

risk.note: Capex intensity and execution/regulatory risks are material but do not presently invalidate the thesis.

confidence.note: Exact primary lineage plus independent current valuation data; operating corroboration remains issuer-heavy.

thesis: Alphabet couples durable AI/cloud demand with vertically expanding compute and energy infrastructure, creating multiple value-capture paths but requiring disciplined conversion of extraordinary capex into cash returns.
keyRisk: Infrastructure spending outruns monetization or is impaired by grid, permitting, regulatory or technology shifts.
nextCatalyst: Cloud backlog conversion and evidence that Intersect/energy investments improve time-to-power and economics.
